newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey preparing steps to lower inflation-minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey preparing steps to lower inflation-minister.

text.p: Turkey's State Minister Gunes Taner, in charge of the economy, said on Wednesday the government was preparing a programme to lower inflation, which he forecast a day ago could hit 100 percent at the end of the year.
"The inflation's trend is at such a stage that if we do not do anything, the uptrend in inflation will pose dangers," Taner told reporters in Istanbul.
"We are preparing a program to change this trend," he said.

Taner told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that he expected annual inflation at year-end to hit 100 percent because of instabilities created by the former coalition government between Islamists and conservatives.
The government's inflation target for the year was 85 percent.
Taner's comments boosted bond prices by about eight percentage points on Wednesday while Istanbul stocks ended the morning session 2.1 percent lower at 1,912.
"What I said was an estimate," Taner said, referring to his comment to Reuters.
"Did I not say before that if we had not raised taxes on some goods the inflation in 1998 would exceed 150 percent? Yes, I did," he said.
"The actual exact figure for the inflation at the end of this year depends on the measures we should take now. There is no reason why we should panic," he said.
